about: a two-page October bank statement for a bakery: eight deposits and six withdrawals across both pages

reads.note: Google Drive v3 file download: GET /drive/v3/files/<id>?fields=mimeType,name (supportsAllDrives), then ?alt=media for the bytes (binary, so tls-intercept). The PDF is a small text stand-in for the scanned statement

connector.none: no connector: a self-hosted Stirling PDF service; the Claude side gets the same response through its HTTP mock

reads.note: HTTP Request v4.2 POST multipart/form-data to the person's self-hosted Stirling PDF (fileInput = the PDF, imageFormat jpg, singleOrMultiple multiple, dpi 300). Stirling answers a zip of one JPEG per page, named <file>_<page>.jpg, as an attachment (content type and disposition as Stirling's web response helper sets them, unverified). The page images here are 850x1100 stand-ins, not 300 dpi

branches: no IF/Switch: two page images → sorted by file name → resized → transcribed one by one → aggregated → one extraction
expect.offline: No write: the run's output is Extract All Deposit Table Rows' items (README P70 result effect), and both chains are model replies (Gemini 1.5 Pro, recorded on the n8n side; one transcription call per page image). Resize Images For AI runs GraphicsMagick in the n8n image. The Stirling PDF host is the person's own container (http://stirling-pdf:8080), reached through the mock
expect.n8nCannotRun: The bench's plain-HTTP proxy path: Split PDF into Images sends the downloaded statement (a disk-stored binary) as multipart to the person's own http:// Stirling host, and through the mock's forward proxy that body arrives malformed (the mock parses a cut-off file part and answers 400); the same request straight to a server, or to an https host through the mock's CONNECT tunnel, is well-formed (PROPOSALS P100). Probed with the Stirling route moved to https, every variant runs to its expected end
